question.text: Mark-to-Market for illiquid securities in a Cat III AIF is typically NOT at full Fair Market Value; the manager must instead apply:

answer.text: The last traded price regardless of volume
A valuation method approved by the registered valuer reflecting illiquidity, e.g., PV of expected realisable proceeds over multiple trading days

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the chapter: 'valuation of illiquid securities shall not be done on the basis of the Fair Market Value of the security. The Investment Manager shall clearly state the Valuation Method adopted by the fund for the valuation of illiquid securities, approved by a registered valuer.' The workbook illustrates one such method as the present value of expected sale proceeds spread over multiple trading days. The Trap: The last traded price is exactly what the rule precludes for illiquid stock; the issuer's book value is unrelated to market realisable value; an arbitrary 50% haircut is not an approved method. Note: Both the requirement (a valuer-approved method) and one illustrative method (PV of realisable proceeds over several days) come directly from the chapter.
